call_points.text: Festive shift from September to October impacted Q2 growth, with a strong recovery anticipated in Q3.
No FY27 revenue growth or net store addition number given; expansion guided only by location availability and returns.
E-commerce grew 39% in FY26 and contributed 12.9% of overall revenue.
FY26 EBITDA margin was 30.3% while the company kept investing in stores, marketing, technology and new formats.
Store closures have historically run at 2-3% of the network; most mature stores are profitable.
Competition remains high across most segments and price points, per management.
FY27 pricing actions will be taken judiciously, weighing demand, competition and cost movements.
Statutory and secretarial audit reports on FY26 carried no qualifications, observations or comments.
FY26 delivered within guidance: PAT mid-teens %, EBITDA high 20s to low 30s, sales growth 15%.
Management is confident of sustaining ~15% year-on-year growth long term, without committing to every quarter.
Input costs are up about 10% overall, with forward buying and six months of inventory cushioning the impact.
Pre-IndAS EBITDA was around 21% and pre-IndAS PAT 15.5% for the full year.
Network reached 1,032 stores with 42 net additions in Q4, including the first two FILA stores.

call_points.text: About 50 stores could open across FILA, Foot Locker, Clarks and MetroActiv, subject to locations and BIS.

The company expects to get supply of complete product range by Q2 FY27 from Clarks and launch EBOs in Q3 FY27.
